dims: So Saul died for his trespass which he committed against Yahweh, because of Yahweh’s word, which he didn’t keep
killed himself (fell on his sword) in the battle at Gilboa
under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh; his bones later in Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father
tx: 1 Sam 13:1 (WEB): thirty years old, reigned forty-two years; Acts 13:21: forty years
items.note: Anointed by Samuel and made king at Gilgal. Samuel–Kings give him no regnal verdict; the line quoted is the Chronicler's judgment on his death.

items.s: king over Israel, not Judah, rival of David
dims: killed on his bed by Rechab and Baanah
his head, in Abner’s grave in Hebron
tx: Ussher's Annals put his making 1055 and his murder 1048 BC; the text gives two years and doesn't say where they fall in David's seven and a half in Hebron
items.note: Abner made him king over Gilead, Ephraim, Benjamin and 'all Israel' from Mahanaim, while the house of Judah followed David in Hebron (2 Sam 2:8-11). His two years sit inside David's seven and a half in Hebron.

dims: David did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes, and didn’t turn away from anything that he commanded him all the days of his life, except only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
died at a good old age
tx: Hebron: seven years and six months (2 Sam 5:5; 2 Sam 2:11; 1 Chr 3:4) or seven years (1 Kgs 2:11; 1 Chr 29:27); Jerusalem: thirty-three years in all of them
Ussher's Annals: king of Judah in Hebron 1055 BC, of all Israel 1048, died 1015
items.note: Anointed king over the house of Judah in Hebron (2 Sam 2:4), then over all Israel (2 Sam 5:3); reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem. His mother is not named.

dims: Solomon did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and didn’t go fully after Yahweh, as David his father did.
items.note: Anointed while David lived (1 Kgs 1:39). Early on he 'loved Yahweh' but sacrificed in the high places (1 Kgs 3:3); in old age his wives turned his heart (1 Kgs 11:4). 1 Chr 3:5 names his mother 'Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel'. His age at accession is not given.

dims: He did that which was evil, because he didn’t set his heart to seek Yahweh.
with his fathers in David’s city
items.note: The kingdom divided at his accession; he reigned over the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah (1 Kgs 12:17). Kings' own verdict (1 Kgs 14:22) is spoken of Judah, not of him.

dims: in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam the son of Nebat
He walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him; and his heart was not perfect with Yahweh his God
items.note: Kings calls him Abijam; Chronicles and Matthew, Abijah. 2 Chr 13:2 names his mother 'Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah', 2 Chr 11:20 'Maacah the daughter of Absalom'. His age at accession is not given.

dims: in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel
Asa did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes, as David his father did. … But the high places were not taken away. Nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect with Yahweh all his days.
died, diseased in his feet, in the forty-first year of his reign
with his fathers in David’s city, in the tomb he had dug for himself
items.note: He removed Maacah 'his mother' from being queen (1 Kgs 15:13); Kings names the same Maacah as Abijam's mother (1 Kgs 15:2). His age at accession is not given.

dims: in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel
He walked in all the way of Asa his father. He didn’t turn away from it, doing that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes. However the high places were not taken away.
with his fathers in his father David’s city
items.note: He made peace with the king of Israel (1 Kgs 22:44) and went to war beside Ahab (1 Kgs 22) and Jehoram of Israel (2 Kgs 3).

dims: in the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Jehoshaphat being king of Judah then
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did Ahab’s house; for he married Ahab’s daughter. He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight.
died of an incurable disease of the bowels
with his fathers in David’s city (Chronicles: but not in the tombs of the kings)
items.note: He married Ahab's daughter, and Edom and Libnah revolted in his days. 'Jehoshaphat being king of Judah then' (2 Kgs 8:16) and 2 Kgs 1:17 point to a coregency with his father. His mother is not named.

dims: one year, from age 22 (2 Kgs 8:26); 42 (2 Chr 22:2)
in the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel
Athaliah the daughter of Omri king of Israel
He walked in the way of Ahab’s house, and did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, as did Ahab’s house
struck down by Jehu's men; fled to Megiddo and died there
in his tomb with his fathers in David’s city
items.note: Killed in Jehu's revolt along with Joram of Israel, whom he had gone to visit. 2 Chr 22:9 tells it differently: caught hiding in Samaria and brought to Jehu.

dims: killed at the horses’ entry to the king’s house, at Jehoiada’s command
items.note: Ahaziah's mother. When he died she usurped Judah and destroyed the royal offspring; only Joash was hidden from her. She is 'the daughter of Omri' (2 Kgs 8:26), but Jehoram married 'Ahab's daughter' (2 Kgs 8:18). No regnal formula: no synchronism, age, verdict or burial.

dims: in the seventh year of Jehu
Jehoash did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes all his days in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him. However the high places were not taken away.
killed by his servants Jozacar and Jehozabad
with his fathers in David’s city (Chronicles: not in the tombs of the kings)
items.note: Hidden six years in the temple from Athaliah, then crowned at seven by Jehoiada the priest. Chronicles says he was killed for the blood of Jehoiada's sons (2 Chr 24:25).

dims: in the second year of Joash son of Joahaz king of Israel
He did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes, yet not like David his father.
at Jerusalem with his fathers in David’s city
items.note: Taken captive by Jehoash of Israel at Beth Shemesh (2 Kgs 14:13). 2 Chr 25:1 spells his mother Jehoaddan, and 2 Chr 25:28 buries him 'in the City of Judah'.

dims: in the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel
He did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes, according to all that his father Amaziah had done. However the high places were not taken away.
with his fathers in David’s city (Chronicles: in the field of burial which belonged to the kings, 'He is a leper')
items.note: Kings mostly calls him Azariah; Chronicles and the prophets, Uzziah. Struck with leprosy, he lived apart while Jotham judged the people (2 Kgs 15:5). 2 Chr 26:3 spells his mother Jechiliah.

dims: in the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel
He did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes. He did according to all that his father Uzziah had done. However the high places were not taken away.
with his fathers in his father David’s city
items.note: Governed for his leprous father (2 Kgs 15:5). 2 Kgs 15:30 dates Pekah's death to 'the twentieth year of Jotham', beyond his sixteen years. 2 Chr 27:1 spells his mother Jerushah.

dims: in the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah
He didn’t do that which was right in Yahweh his God’s eyes, like David his father.
with his fathers in David’s city (Chronicles: in Jerusalem, not in the tombs of the kings of Israel)
items.note: He made his son pass through the fire (2 Kgs 16:3). The verdict is a negative 'didn't do that which was right'. His mother is not named.

dims: in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel
He did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes, according to all that David his father had done.
in the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David
items.note: Samaria fell in his sixth year (2 Kgs 18:10). 2 Chr 29:1 names his mother Abijah. Kings does not say where he was buried.

dims: He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, after the abominations of the nations whom Yahweh cast out before the children of Israel.
in the garden of his own house, in the garden of Uzza
items.note: The longest reign in either kingdom. Only Chronicles tells of his captivity in Babylon, his repentance and his return (2 Chr 33:11-13).

dims: Meshullemeth the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, as Manasseh his father did.
killed in his own house by his servants
in his tomb in the garden of Uzza
items.note: The people of the land killed the conspirators and made Josiah king (2 Kgs 21:24).

dims: Jedidah the daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath
He did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes, and walked in all the way of David his father, and didn’t turn away to the right hand or to the left.
killed by Pharaoh Necoh at Megiddo
in his own tomb (Chronicles: in the tombs of his fathers)
items.note: 'There was no king like him before him' (2 Kgs 23:25).

dims: Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, according to all that his fathers had done.
put in bonds by Pharaoh Necoh and taken to Egypt, where he died
items.note: Made king by the people of the land. Jeremiah calls him Shallum (Jer 22:11), and 1 Chr 3:15 lists Shallum as Josiah's fourth son.

dims: Zebidah the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, according to all that his fathers had done.
died (Chronicles: Nebuchadnezzar bound him in fetters to carry him to Babylon)
items.note: Pharaoh Necoh made Eliakim king and renamed him; he served Nebuchadnezzar three years, then rebelled (2 Kgs 24:1). No burial is recorded; Jeremiah foretold 'the burial of a donkey' (Jer 22:19).

dims: three months, from age 18 (2 Kgs 24:8); 8 (2 Chr 36:9)
Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, according to all that his father had done.
went out to the king of Babylon and was carried away to Babylon
tx: three months (2 Kgs 24:8); three months and ten days (2 Chr 36:9)
items.note: Released from prison by Evilmerodach in the thirty-seventh year of his captivity and fed at the king's table all his days (2 Kgs 25:27-30).

dims: Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
captured fleeing Jerusalem, blinded and carried to Babylon in fetters
items.note: Jehoiachin's father's brother, made king and renamed by Nebuchadnezzar (2 Kgs 24:17); full brother of Jehoahaz (same mother). He died in prison in Babylon (Jer 52:11).

dims: but have done evil above all who were before you, and have gone and made for yourself other gods, molten images
items.note: Israel made him king when the ten tribes broke from Rehoboam (1 Kgs 12:20); no synchronism is given. He set up the golden calves at Bethel and Dan (1 Kgs 12:28-29), 'the sins of Jeroboam' by which every later king of Israel is judged.

dims: in the second year of Asa king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and walked in the way of his father
items.note: Killed at Gibbethon while besieging it; Baasha then wiped out the house of Jeroboam (1 Kgs 15:29).

dims: In the third year of Asa king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and walked in the way of Jeroboam
items.note: Of the house of Issachar (1 Kgs 15:27); reigned in Tirzah and fought Asa all his days, building Ramah against Judah.

dims: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah
for all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, which they sinned, and with which they made Israel to sin
items.note: Killed while drunk in the house of Arza in Tirzah. His verdict is not the usual 'evil in Yahweh’s sight' formula but the charge of 16:13.

dims: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah
for his sins which he sinned in doing that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, in walking in the way of Jeroboam
burned the king's house over himself and died
items.note: Elah's captain of half his chariots (1 Kgs 16:9); he destroyed the house of Baasha, and the army at Gibbethon made Omri king against him.

tx: Derived: the four years from Asa's 27th year, when Omri was made king in the camp, to his 31st, when Omri reigned alone (1 Kgs 16:15-23)
items.note: Rival king, not in the regular succession: half the people followed Tibni and half Omri, until Omri's side prevailed and Tibni died. The text gives no length, synchronism or verdict.

dims: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah
Omri did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and dealt wickedly above all who were before him.
items.note: The captain of the army, made king in the camp at Gibbethon the day Zimri killed Elah (1 Kgs 16:16), so in Asa's 27th year; his twelve years are counted from then, 'six years in Tirzah' (16:23). He bought the hill of Samaria and built the city (16:24).

dims: In the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah
Ahab the son of Omri did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight above all that were before him.
killed by an arrow in battle at Ramoth Gilead
items.note: Married Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians and served Baal (1 Kgs 16:31); the age of Elijah. 1 Kgs 22:40 also says he 'slept with his fathers'.

dims: in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and walked in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother
died after falling through the lattice of his upper room
items.note: He sent to Baal Zebub of Ekron and died as Elijah foretold; he had no son, so his brother Jehoram followed (2 Kgs 1:17). 1 Kgs 22:52 mentions 'his mother' without naming her.

dims: in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, but not like his father, and like his mother, for he put away the pillar of Baal that his father had made.
items.note: The WEB calls him Jehoram in 2 Kgs 1:17 and 3:1 and Joram in 2 Kgs 8-9. A second synchronism puts his accession 'in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah' (2 Kgs 1:17). His body was thrown onto Naboth's plot at Jezreel (2 Kgs 9:25-26); no burial is told.

dims: Because you have done well in executing that which is right in my eyes ... But Jehu took no heed to walk in the law of Yahweh, the God of Israel, with all his heart.
items.note: Anointed by a son of the prophets at Elisha's word (2 Kgs 9:1-6); no synchronism, since he killed Jehoram of Israel and Ahaziah of Judah on the same day. He destroyed Baal out of Israel but kept the golden calves (10:28-29); promised descendants to the fourth generation (10:30).

dims: In the twenty-third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat
items.note: Israel was oppressed by Hazael and Benhadad of Syria; he begged Yahweh and was heard (2 Kgs 13:3-5).

dims: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight. He didn’t depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat
Samaria, with the kings of Israel
items.note: The WEB calls him Jehoash in 2 Kgs 13:10 and 14:8-16 and Joash in 13:9-13, 14:1 and 2 Chr 25. He defeated Amaziah of Judah at Beth Shemesh and broke down Jerusalem's wall (2 Kgs 14:11-14). His closing formula appears twice (13:12-13 and 14:15-16).

dims: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight. He didn’t depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat
items.note: Jeroboam II. He restored Israel's border from the entrance of Hamath to the sea of the Arabah, as Jonah the son of Amittai foretold (2 Kgs 14:25). 1 Chr 5:17 mentions 'the days of Jeroboam king of Israel' but tells nothing of his reign.

dims: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, as his fathers had done.
items.note: The last of Jehu's line, fulfilling the promise of four generations (2 Kgs 15:12).

dims: in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah
items.note: Not the Shallum of Judah (Jehoahaz son of Josiah). His synchronism names Judah's king Uzziah, where the verses around it say Azariah.

dims: In the thirty ninth year of Azariah king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight. He didn’t depart all his days from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat
items.note: He came up from Tirzah, killed Shallum, and paid Pul king of Assyria a thousand talents of silver (2 Kgs 15:19-20).

dims: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight. He didn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat
items.note: Killed in the fortress of the king's house in Samaria by his captain Pekah, with fifty Gileadites.

dims: In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight. He didn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat
items.note: Tiglath Pileser took Galilee and Gilead in his days (2 Kgs 15:29); with Rezin of Syria he besieged Ahaz in Jerusalem (16:5). Thiele makes his twenty years overlap Menahem's and Pekahiah's reigns.

dims: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, yet not as the kings of Israel who were before him.
seized and bound in prison by the king of Assyria; Samaria taken in his ninth year
items.note: The last king of Israel. He killed Pekah (2 Kgs 15:30), became Shalmaneser's servant, then conspired with So king of Egypt; Samaria fell after a three-year siege and Israel was carried away to Assyria (17:3-6; 18:9-11).

dims: in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah
items.note: Son of Amoz. Kings also call Uzziah Azariah (2 Kgs 15:1; Uzziah at 2 Kgs 15:13). The histories show him with Hezekiah (2 Kgs 19-20; 2 Chr 32:20) and say he wrote Uzziah's acts (2 Chr 26:22).

dims: in the days of Josiah ... in the thirteenth year of his reign ... Jehoiakim ... to the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah
627–588 BC, from the years these verses give
items.note: Son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth (Jer 1:1). The opening leaves out Jehoahaz and Jehoiachin. The book addresses Jehoiachin as Coniah (Jer 22:24). Chronicles has him lamenting Josiah (2 Chr 35:25), and Zedekiah 'didn't humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet' (2 Chr 36:12).

dims: the fifth year of king Jehoiachin's captivity
595–575 BC, from the years these verses give
items.note: Priest, son of Buzi, among the captives by the river Chebar. The text gives no anchor for the 'thirtieth year' of Ezek 1:1. The book dates by the years of Jehoiachin's captivity, not by a reign.

dims: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem
606–534 BC, from the years these verses give
items.note: Renamed Belteshazzar (Dan 1:7). Dan 1:21 says he 'continued even to the first year of king Cyrus'. The opening verse dates Nebuchadnezzar's siege, not Daniel's call.

dims: in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel
810–698 BC, from the years these verses give
tx: Uzziah (Judah), Jotham (Judah), Ahaz (Judah), Hezekiah (Judah), Jeroboam son of Joash (Israel)
items.note: Son of Beeri. He prophesied to Israel, yet four of the five kings named are Judah's. The only Israelite king named is Jeroboam son of Joash (Jeroboam II).
Undated: Joel 1:1 names only 'Joel, the son of Pethuel' and no king. Realm judah is an inference from the book's address to Judah and Jerusalem (Joel 3:1).

dims: in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake
810–784 BC, from the years these verses give
items.note: A herdsman of Tekoa who saw 'concerning Israel'. 'Two years before the earthquake' is a narrower date than the reigns.
Undated: Obad 1:1 names no king. The oracle is about Edom. Realm judah is an inference from Edom's part when lots were cast 'for Jerusalem' (Obad 1:11). Not Ahab's servant Obadiah of 1 Kgs 18.

dims: according to ... his servant Jonah the son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gath Hepher
items.note: Jonah 1:1 names no king. The date comes from 2 Kgs 14:25, where Jeroboam son of Joash restored Israel's border as Jonah had foretold. His ministry in the book is to Nineveh.

dims: in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem
items.note: 'Micah the Morashtite'. Jer 26:18 recalls that he prophesied in the days of Hezekiah. Not Micaiah son of Imlah (1 Kgs 22).
Undated: Nah 1:1 ('A revelation about Nineveh ... Nahum the Elkoshite') names no king. Realm judah is an inference from Nah 1:15 ('Keep your feasts, Judah!').
Undated: Hab 1:1 names no king. The book foresees the Chaldeans being raised up (Hab 1:6). Realm judah is an inference.

dims: in the days of Josiah, the son of Amon, king of Judah
items.note: His genealogy goes back to 'Hezekiah' (Zeph 1:1). The verse does not call that Hezekiah a king, so he is not listed as a tied king.

dims: In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month
520 BC, from the years these verses give
items.note: Hag 1:1 says only 'Darius the king'. 'Darius king of Persia' is from Ezra 4:24. He spoke to Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest.

dims: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius
520–518 BC, from the years these verses give
items.note: Zech 1:1 makes him 'the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo'; Ezra 5:1 calls him 'the son of Iddo'. Persia from Ezra 4:24. Not Zechariah son of Jehoiada (2 Chr 24:20).
Undated: Mal 1:1 names no king. Realm return is an inference from 'your governor' (Mal 1:8) and the working altar.

dims: Samuel took the vial of oil, and poured it on his head ... Yahweh sent me to anoint you to be king
1100–1060 BC, from the years these verses give
items.note: 'Established to be a prophet of Yahweh' (1 Sam 3:20). He calls himself the seer (1 Sam 9:19). Also the last judge (1 Sam 7:15). He anointed Saul and David and died before David reigned (1 Sam 25:1).
Called both prophet and seer, 'the king's seer' (2 Chr 29:25).

dims: the king said to Nathan the prophet ... Let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him
items.note: Gave David the dynasty oracle (2 Sam 7), rebuked him over Uriah (2 Sam 12), and helped anoint Solomon (1 Kgs 1:34).

dims: when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him
items.note: 'Ahijah the Shilonite'. In Solomon's reign he tore the garment in twelve and gave Jeroboam ten pieces. Later he foretold the death of Jeroboam's son Abijah (1 Kgs 14).

dims: Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah
items.note: Called 'the man of God' (1 Kgs 12:22) and 'the prophet' (2 Chr 12:5). In Chronicles he spoke when Shishak came up 'in the fifth year of king Rehoboam' (2 Chr 12:2).

items.n: the man of God from Judah
dims: a man of God came out of Judah ... Jeroboam was standing by the altar ... a son will be born to David's house, Josiah by name
items.note: Unnamed. He cried against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel and named Josiah, who fulfilled the word (2 Kgs 23:16-17). The old prophet of Bethel (1 Kgs 13:11) is also unnamed and is not listed.

dims: Yahweh's word came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha ... said to king Jehoshaphat
items.note: He spoke against Baasha of Israel, then rebuked Jehoshaphat of Judah, so he spoke in both kingdoms. Son of Hanani the seer. Not king Jehu son of Nimshi.

dims: Elijah the Tishbite ... said to Ahab ... A letter came to him from Elijah the prophet
items.note: 'Elijah the Tishbite'. His letter to Jehoram of Judah (2 Chr 21:12) is his only tie to a Judahite king. He went up by a whirlwind (2 Kgs 2:11).

dims: Jehoram the son of Ahab began to reign ... Elisha the son of Shaphat ... is here ... Joash the king of Israel came down to him
tx: Jehoram (Israel), Jehoshaphat (Judah), Jehu (Israel), Joash (Israel), Benhadad (Syria), Hazael (Syria)
items.note: Anointed 'to be prophet in your place' (1 Kgs 19:16). The WEB calls Ahab's son Jehoram (2 Kgs 3:1) and Joram (2 Kgs 8:16; 9:14), and the king of 2 Kgs 13:14 Joash (Jehoash at 2 Kgs 13:10). Elisha sent a son of the prophets to anoint Jehu (2 Kgs 9:1). He died under Joash (2 Kgs 13:20).

dims: Micaiah the son of Imlah; but I hate him ... Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah
items.note: 1 Kgs 22:8 has 'Imlah'; 2 Chr 18:7 has 'Imla'. 1 Kgs 22:8 calls the king only 'king of Israel'. Ahab is named at 1 Kgs 22:20 and 2 Chr 18:3. The text never calls Micaiah 'the prophet'; he is the one 'by whom we may inquire of Yahweh'.

dims: The Spirit of God came on Azariah the son of Oded: and he went out to meet Asa
items.note: 2 Chr 15:8 attributes the same prophecy to 'Oded the prophet' (the WEB text as it stands). Asa's assembly followed 'in the fifteenth year of Asa's reign' (2 Chr 15:10). Not the Oded of 2 Chr 28:9.

dims: At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah
items.note: He rebuked Asa for relying on the king of Syria, after Baasha's move 'in the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign' (2 Chr 16:1). Asa put him in prison (2 Chr 16:10). Father of Jehu the prophet (2 Chr 19:2).

dims: Yahweh's Spirit came on Jahaziel ... and you, king Jehoshaphat
items.note: Levite of the sons of Asaph, 'son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah'. The text never calls him a prophet; the Spirit came on him and he spoke 'Yahweh says'.

dims: Eliezer the son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat
items.note: He prophesied against Jehoshaphat's shipping alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel. 'Prophesied' is the text's word; he is not given the title prophet.

dims: The Spirit of God came on Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest ... Joash the king
items.note: A priest. The text does not call him a prophet: 24:19 says the king 'sent prophets to them', and the Spirit came on Zechariah to speak 'Thus says God'. Stoned by Joash's command.

dims: a prophet of Yahweh was there, whose name was Oded
items.note: At Samaria he met Pekah's army returning with Judahite captives in Ahaz's reign, and the captives were sent back. Not Oded father of Azariah (2 Chr 15:1, 8).

dims: In the eighteenth year of king Josiah ... went to Huldah the prophetess
items.note: The genealogy of her husband Shallum differs between the books: 'son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas' (2 Kgs 22:14) and 'son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah' (2 Chr 34:22).

dims: a man who prophesied in Yahweh's name, Uriah the son of Shemaiah ... Jehoiakim the king ... killed him
items.note: Of Kiriath Jearim. His story is in Jeremiah, not Samuel-Kings-Chronicles. He fled to Egypt and was brought back and killed by Jehoiakim. Not Uriah the Hittite.

dims: the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam ... the histories of ... Iddo the seer ... the commentary of the prophet Iddo
items.note: Named only as the author of written sources for Solomon, Rehoboam and Abijah, with his visions 'concerning Jeroboam'. He never acts in the narrative.

dims: David ... set apart ... sons of ... Heman ... who were to prophesy ... Heman the king's seer
items.note: A Levite singer. Grandson of Samuel (1 Chr 6:33). A temple-music seer, not an oracle-bearing prophet.

dims: Asaph, who prophesied at the order of the king ... the words of David, and of Asaph the seer
items.note: A Levite singer under David. Hezekiah's Levites sang 'the words of David, and of Asaph the seer' (2 Chr 29:30), so he is tied to Hezekiah only as a source of the songs.

dims: Jeduthun, who prophesied in giving thanks ... Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's seer
items.note: A Levite singer under David. In 2 Chr 35:15 it is unclear whether 'the king's seer' applies to Jeduthun alone or to all three.

items.s: Ammon, as Saul came to the throne
dims: Nahash the Ammonite came up ... they made Saul king
c. 1050, approximate (conventional date for Saul's accession; no fixed synchronism)
items.note: Nahash the Ammonite encamps against Jabesh Gilead; Saul is made king at Gilgal.

dims: a full year and four months
c. 1012-1011, approximate (the 16 months before Saul's death, conventionally c. 1011/1010)
items.note: David passes over to Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath.

dims: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David
c. 1000-980, approximate; Josephus' Tyrian list (Against Apion 1.117-126) puts Hiram I's accession c. 980
items.note: Hiram king of Tyre sends cedar, carpenters and masons to build David a house.

dims: David struck also Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah
items.note: David strikes Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

dims: Hanun his son reigned in his place
items.note: Nahash king of Ammon dies; David sends comfort to Hanun his son.

items.s: Tyre, as Solomon came to the throne
dims: they had anointed him king in the place of his father
971/970 (Thiele, Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings, 3rd ed.: Solomon 971-931; temple begun in his 4th year, 967/966, 1 Kgs 6:1)
items.note: Hiram king of Tyre sends his servants to Solomon and supplies cedar and cypress for Yahweh's house.

dims: At the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the two houses
c. 947/946 (Thiele: twenty years from the temple's start in 967/966)
items.note: Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.

dims: an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon
items.note: Rezon the son of Eliada reigns in Damascus, an adversary all the days of Solomon.

dims: was in Egypt until the death of Solomon
before 931 (Thiele: Solomon's death 931/930); Shoshenq I reigned c. 945-924 (Kitchen, Third Intermediate Period in Egypt)
items.note: Jeroboam flees into Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt.

dims: In the fifth year of king Rehoboam
925 (Kitchen, Third Intermediate Period in Egypt; Thiele 926/925)
items.note: Shishak king of Egypt comes up against Jerusalem and takes the treasures.

dims: in the fifteenth year of Asa's reign ... of the plunder which they had brought
items.note: Zerah the Ethiopian comes against Asa at Mareshah and is routed to Gerar.

dims: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha ... went up
c. 895/894 (Thiele, reading the 36th year from the division of the kingdom)
items.note: Asa sends silver and gold to Ben Hadad king of Syria, who strikes the cities of Israel.

dims: He sent messengers to Ahab king of Israel
c. 857-855, approximate (before the three years of peace and Ahab's death in 853, 1 Kgs 22:1; Thiele)
items.note: Ben Hadad the king of Syria, with thirty-two kings, besieges Samaria; Ahab defeats him.

dims: At the return of the year
c. 856-855, approximate (three years before Ahab's death in 853; Thiele)
items.note: Ben Hadad goes up to Aphek, is defeated, and makes a covenant with Ahab.

dims: when Ahab was dead, the king of Moab rebelled
853/852 (Thiele: Ahab died 853, the year of Qarqar per Shalmaneser III's Kurkh Monolith); the revolt is also on the Mesha Stele
items.note: Mesha king of Moab rebels against the king of Israel.

dims: King Jehoram went out of Samaria at that time
c. 852-848, approximate (Thiele: Jehoram/Joram of Israel 852-841, Jehoshaphat died 848)
items.note: King Jehoram, with Jehoshaphat, marches against the king of Moab.

dims: In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab
841 (Thiele; Jehu paid tribute to Shalmaneser III in 841, Black Obelisk)
items.note: Joram and Ahaziah war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth Gilead; Joram is wounded.

dims: In those days Yahweh began to cut away parts of Israel
c. 837-814 (after Shalmaneser III's last western campaign, 838/837; Cogan and Tadmor, II Kings, Anchor Bible; Jehu 841-814 Thiele)
items.note: Hazael strikes Israel in all its borders, east of the Jordan.

dims: Then Hazael king of Syria went up
c. 815, approximate (late 9th century; the destruction of Gath at Tell es-Safi; Jehoash of Judah 835-796 Thiele)
items.note: Hazael king of Syria takes Gath; Jehoash king of Judah buys him off with the temple treasures.
Hazael king of Syria oppresses Israel.
Hazael dies; Jehoash of Israel strikes Benhadad the son of Hazael three times and recovers the cities.

dims: Menahem gave Pul one thousand talents of silver
738 (tribute of Menahem of Samaria in Tiglath-pileser III's annals; Tadmor, Inscriptions of Tiglath-pileser III)
items.note: Pul the king of Assyria comes against the land; Menahem gives him a thousand talents of silver.

dims: They besieged Ahaz, but could not overcome him
734 (Syro-Ephraimite war; Cogan and Tadmor, II Kings, Anchor Bible)
items.note: Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah besiege Ahaz in Jerusalem; Rezin recovers Elath.

dims: I am your servant and your son
734 (Tadmor, Inscriptions of Tiglath-pileser III: 'Jehoahaz of Judah' among the tributaries)
items.note: Ahaz sends messengers and a present to Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria.

dims: In the days of Pekah king of Israel
733-732 (Tadmor, Inscriptions of Tiglath-pileser III; Assyrian eponym chronicle)
items.note: Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria takes Galilee and all the land of Naphtali, and carries them captive.

dims: went up against Damascus, and took it ... and killed Rezin
732 (Assyrian eponym chronicle: campaigns against Damascus 733-732; Tadmor)
items.note: The king of Assyria takes Damascus and kills Rezin; Ahaz meets Tiglath Pileser at Damascus.

dims: Hoshea became his servant, and brought him tribute
727-725 (Shalmaneser V reigned 727-722; Cogan and Tadmor, II Kings, Anchor Bible)
items.note: Shalmaneser king of Assyria comes up against Hoshea, who becomes his servant.

dims: he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt
c. 725/724 (Cogan and Tadmor, II Kings, Anchor Bible; So often identified with Osorkon IV, Kitchen)
items.note: Hoshea sends messengers to So king of Egypt; the king of Assyria imprisons him.

dims: In the fourth year of king Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea
725 (Cogan and Tadmor, II Kings, Anchor Bible; Thiele 725/724)
items.note: Shalmaneser king of Assyria comes up against Samaria and besieges it.

dims: In the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea
722 (Babylonian Chronicle 1 i 28, Grayson ABC: Shalmaneser V ravaged Samaria; Thiele 723/722; Sargon II claims the deportation, 720)
items.note: Samaria is taken and Israel carried away to Assyria.

dims: in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah
701 (Sennacherib's annals, third campaign, Rassam Cylinder and Taylor Prism; Thiele 701)
items.note: Sennacherib king of Assyria comes up against all the fortified cities of Judah.

dims: Tirhakah king of Ethiopia ... has come out to fight against you
701 (same campaign; Taharqa reigned 690-664 as king, Kitchen, Third Intermediate Period in Egypt)
items.note: Tirhakah king of Ethiopia comes out to fight against Sennacherib.

dims: At that time Berodach Baladan ... king of Babylon, sent letters
c. 703, or c. 713-711 (Merodach-baladan II ruled Babylon 721-710 and in 703; Brinkman; Cogan and Tadmor, II Kings, Anchor Bible)
items.note: Berodach Baladan king of Babylon sends letters and a present to Hezekiah after his sickness.

dims: In his days Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt went up
609 (Babylonian Chronicle 3, Grayson ABC: Egypt and Assyria at Harran, 609)
items.note: Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt goes up to the Euphrates and kills Josiah at Megiddo.

dims: he reigned three months ... Pharaoh Necoh put him in bonds
items.note: Pharaoh Necoh puts Jehoahaz in bonds at Riblah and makes Eliakim king as Jehoiakim.

dims: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up
604, rebellion c. 601 (Babylonian Chronicle 5, BM 21946, Grayson ABC: Hatti campaign 604, clash with Egypt 601)
items.note: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes up; Jehoiakim becomes his servant three years, then rebels.

dims: the king of Babylon captured him in the eighth year of his reign
597 (Babylonian Chronicle 5, BM 21946, Grayson ABC: Jerusalem taken 2 Adar, 15/16 March 597)
items.note: Jehoiachin goes out to the king of Babylon and is carried to Babylon; Zedekiah made king.

dims: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day
items.note: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army encamp against Jerusalem.

dims: besieged until the eleventh year of king Zedekiah. On the ninth day of the fourth month
items.note: A breach is made in the city; Zedekiah is captured and brought to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

dims: which was the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar
items.note: Nebuzaradan, servant of the king of Babylon, burns Yahweh's house and Jerusalem.

items.s: Babylon, Jehoiachin's 37th year of his captivity
dims: In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin
561 (Amel-Marduk acceded October 562; the 12th month falls in spring 561; Parker and Dubberstein, Babylonian Chronology)
items.note: Evilmerodach king of Babylon lifts up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison.

dims: in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia
538 (Babylon fell October 539; Cyrus's first regnal year over Babylon from Nisan 538; Parker and Dubberstein, Babylonian Chronology)
items.note: Cyrus king of Persia makes a proclamation to build Yahweh's house in Jerusalem.

dims: The land had rest forty years
Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia, eight years
the land had rest eighty years
Eglon the king of Moab (with the children of Ammon and Amalek), eighteen years

items.note: The text gives him no tribe and no years.

dims: the land had rest forty years
Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor (captain Sisera), twenty years
The land had rest forty years in the days of Gideon

items.note: The text never calls him a judge: the men of Shechem made him king (Judg 9:6), and he was prince over Israel three years.

dims: the Philistines and the children of Ammon, eighteen years

items.note: His twenty years were in the days of the Philistines (Judg 15:20), inside their forty.

dims: He had judged Israel forty years
items.note: Not in the book of Judges; 1 Sam 4:18 says he judged Israel forty years.

dims: Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life
